resources.string: Understand your phone. Review local findings.
Some checks could not finish. Refresh to retry.
This check could not finish. Use its check button to retry.

Checks stay on this phone. Nothing is deleted or changed. Share report exports a redacted technical report only when you choose to share it. App names, VPN keys, tokens and browsing history are excluded.
Declared boot capability, not proof that an app ran.

Without privileged access, Android does not provide live CPU or RAM rankings for other apps. The measurements below cover storage and foreground time separately. Android app settings can help you review battery use, permissions and storage for each app; options vary by phone.
CPU is a short VirtuVPN process sample: 100% equals one logical CPU and includes diagnostic work. Android restricts live CPU and RAM rankings for other apps.
Android uses RAM for caching. Low available memory alone does not prove a problem; the Android memory-pressure signal is shown separately.
This is the internal data volume. Android Storage shows media and other storage categories. This screen never deletes files.

Optional: allow Usage access in Android to measure storage and recent foreground time of visible launcher apps. Sizes and usage records are read locally; app names and activity records stay on this screen. This does not grant access to private files or live CPU/RAM rankings.
Storage percentages use the total app + data size successfully measured in this check, including measured apps outside the top eight. They are not shares of all phone storage or CPU/RAM.
Android record period: %1$s – %2$s. Recent daily records can cover a wider period than the requested day.

Time percentages compare foreground time across visible apps with records, including apps outside the top eight. They are not CPU, RAM or battery consumption. Android may omit or delay records, and multitasking can overlap.
No usable foreground records were returned. This does not mean that other apps used no resources.

Largest apps in this measured sample; hidden apps, other user profiles, media and system files are excluded. Up to 64 visible apps are measured per check, with a time limit. Cache is already included in app data.
App storage insights require Android 8 or later. You can use Android Storage instead.
Review visible apps that declare the boot permission or a boot receiver. This check reads local metadata; it does not start, stop or disable apps.

An enabled boot receiver can respond to Android startup; it does not prove that the app actually ran, is still running or is harmful. Boot permission alone is weaker evidence. Android may hide apps or receivers, and other profiles are excluded. Up to 512 visible apps are checked with a time limit; all collected startup entries can be browsed in pages of 20. Review unfamiliar apps in Android settings; background schedules and other startup mechanisms are not fully covered.
Matching entries: %1$d · Collected: %2$d. Filters change this list only; collection evidence is shown above.
No entries match this search and filter. Clear the search or select All apps.
No boot-capable apps were identified in this visible sample. Hidden apps and other startup mechanisms remain unverified.
This Android settings screen is unavailable on this device.
Usage access was not granted. The basic checks remain available.
